title: LIN-4349 P3: landed work makes a Periodical lane read landed (merged-events read, self-exclusion)
description:
## As asked

## This piece: P3 of 4 (may be built after P1; merges only after P2)

Landed work becomes an input to the existing lane-state fold as a new state, `landed`. P3 merges after P2 so that no template that still mints is ever made due sooner.

### Pre-check (do first)

* Confirm that merged close-out events are being recorded. Look for a `merged: true` event for PR #2361 / LIN-4376 through `CloseOutEventsStore.listForIssue`.
* If there is none, fixing the recording is in scope: fix the cause, not a workaround. Find which of `createPipelineMergeRecorder`'s preconditions failed (no workspace id, no installation token, or the Done not written through the proxy) and record it on LIN-4349.

### Files and approach (from the approved plan)

* `lib/close-out-events-store.js`**:** a bounded merged-events read covering the 30-day horizon.
  * Follow the error-swallowing sibling reads (`listForIssue`, `findMergedByPr` return `[]`/`null`), not `firstPressAt`'s throwing style.
  * A failed read supplies no landings, so the lane fails toward `recent`.
* **Wiring (builder note 1):** thread `closeOutEventsStore` through `server.js` → `createProxyRoutes` → `createComputeRoutes` (`routes/proxy-compute.js`).
  * Witness the production wiring, not just test injection: a test that reads `server.js`, as other wiring checks do, or a one-time log when the route runs without a store.
  * A `null` default with only injected tests is the silent-drop shape this must avoid.
* `lib/periodical-runs.js foldPeriodicalRuns`**:** takes landings as data (repo from the PR URL, merge time, issue identifier). It stays pure, with `now` injected, and never reads a store.
  * A lane reads `landed` only when all of these hold:
    * it is `scope: 'repo'`;
    * it would otherwise read `recent`;
    * there is no queued row;
    * a same-repo landing is newer than its last run;
    * at least `LANDED_MIN_GAP_MS` (one day) has passed since its last run.
  * Cadence still yields `due`.
  * A null lane matches any repo; a named lane matches equivalent repo spellings.
  * The top level reads `landed` when it would read `recent` and any lane reads `landed`.
* **Self-exclusion (B1):**
  * Ignore landings whose issue is named by any Periodical evidence row.
  * Add `issueIdentifier` to `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION` (`lib/dispatch-store.js`); the history projection inherits it.
  * Comment beside the exclusion that it depends on Stage-2 rows naming the review issue and carrying `periodicalId`, through the kickoff's opening stamp and `resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker` (LIN-2575).
* **Also update:** `lib/proxy-instructions.js` (the state union), `docs/architecture/source-map.md` (about line 287), and the kickoff first act's state read where needed.
  * Remove the unused fold/projection imports from `routes/proxy.js` (about lines 84–85, builder note 5).
* **Out of scope:** scan-due rendering (`lib/render-observation.js`, `public/observation.js`), and a post-merge hook, scheduler entrance or server-side PR-file join.

### Acceptance and witnesses

* The existing `tests/unit/periodical-runs.test.js` passes unchanged.
* New fold cases:
  * a lane past cadence with landings reads `due`;
  * a queue row beats a landing;
  * an older landing leaves the lane `recent`;
  * a landing inside the one-day gap leaves the lane `recent`;
  * a failed events read gives `recent`;
  * a landing on a Periodical-named issue leaves the lane `recent`;
  * null and named lane repo matching.
* **Route-level real-store witness:** seed a Periodical history row for issue X and a merged close-out event for X, call `GET /api/proxy/periodicals`, and assert the lane stays `recent`. This must fail without the projection change.
* A production wiring witness for `closeOutEventsStore`.
* The pre-check outcome is recorded on LIN-4349.

**Parent:** LIN-4349, "The Periodicals run when work lands, and feed the look-first step". Read the parent's description in full: the `## As asked` block (the person's words, unchanged), and the `## Implementation Plan` (rev 2). The approving plan review is comment `b79ff49e-c3db-46e1-8071-8d9c89402097` on LIN-4349; its "Notes for the builder" are part of this piece where they name it.

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course at the cause and say so on LIN-4349.

**Grounding commit:** `110e35e053ec6ef181f4e230111c6b7f0ade7d9f` (main, 2026-11-08). Main had not moved when this was split (checked 2026-11-08 10:1x UTC). Re-check `git log 110e35e0..main` for the paths below before building.

Session fit: fits one session

Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4349's approving plan-review (comment b79ff49e-c3db-46e1-8071-8d9c89402097, rev 2)

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Outcome (close-out, 2026-11-08)

Implemented and merged in PR [#2376](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2376>) (merge `3272fe4a`, deployed). Built as the approved plan described, with no deviations:

* a bounded merged-events read;
* production wiring of `closeOutEventsStore` to `GET /api/proxy/periodicals`;
* a pure fold with the `landed` lane state;
* B1 self-exclusion through the dispatch projection;
* the state-union listings updated.

Post-deploy, four idle repo-scoped lanes read `landed`. The full history (builder, review and close-out) is in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
**LIN-4381 (P3): PR open, CI green. Not merged; review and close-out own merge and Done.**

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2376, head `d4117ba7d35168a7faa80d28d166ed72edbc0d9e`, rebased on main `f0388614`. Mergeable.

**CI on `d4117ba7`: 7/7 green.** Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan (source), CI success.

**What landed in the PR (6 commits)**
- `CloseOutEventsStore.listMergedSince`: a bounded read of merged events since the 30-day horizon. Merge time is `prMergedAt`, capped at 500, newest first, and it never throws: a failed read returns `[]`, so lanes fail toward `recent`. No new index, because this is LIN-3713's named unindexed shape.
- `closeOutEventsStore` is threaded through `server.js` → `createProxyRoutes` → `createComputeRoutes` → `GET /api/proxy/periodicals` (builder note 1). A source-reading test pins each hop, and the route warns once if it runs without the store.
- `foldPeriodicalRuns` gains `landed`. A lane that would read `recent` reads `landed` when:
  - the template is `scope: 'repo'`;
  - the lane has no queued row;
  - a same-repo landing merged after its last run;
  - at least one day (`LANDED_MIN_GAP_MS`) has passed since that run.
  
  `due` still wins, and `never` is untouched. The top level reads `landed` when it would read `recent` and a lane does.
- Self-exclusion (B1): a landing on an issue any Periodical row names is ignored. `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION` now grants `issueIdentifier`.
- `routes/proxy.js`'s unused imports are removed (builder note 5).
- `landed` is now named in `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, the route comment, the source map, the general kickoff's first act ("rank it as `recent`" until LIN-4382), `docs/autopilot.md`, `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` and `docs/passage-planner-prompt.md`.

**Witnesses, each seen failing first**
- The wiring test failed with each hop removed.
- The projection round trip failed 4 of 4 without the grant.
- The fold cases: the 7 that expect `landed` fail against main's fold, and disabling each guard in turn was caught by a test.
- The route test over real stores failed with `'landed' !== 'recent'` with `issueIdentifier` removed from the projection. Its positive pair fails against main's fold.
- `tests/unit/periodical-runs.test.js` is unchanged and passes (79/79).

**Local full unit suite:** 24,669 of 24,670 pass. The one failure is environmental: `scripts/code-shape/wrappers.test.mjs`, caused by the runner's `TMPDIR`. It fails the same way on main and passes on a neutral `TMPDIR`. CI's unit job is green.

**Pre-check:** not observable from the builder session (LIN-4349 comment `68476ed5`).

**Still open:**
- Recording of merged events hasn't been observed live.
- Plan risk 4 (`landed` never fires) stays open until P4 and the post-deploy check. After deploy, the first proxy-written Done of a merged PR should show a `landed` lane in `GET /periodicals`.

## Review — LIN-4381

Reviewed PR [#2376](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2376), head `d4117ba7d35168a7faa80d28d166ed72edbc0d9e` (contains main `f0388614`, mergeable).

CI: green on `d4117ba7`, 7/7 (Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success).

### Against what was asked
- **Pre-check.** Not settled. The builder's LIN-4349 comment `68476ed5` is accurate: no proxy-reachable route reads `close-out-events`. The only readers are `lib/task-page-loader.js` (session-authed) and the milestone funnel. I confirmed from this session that it can't be observed either. The ledger carries it (item 1).
- **`listMergedSince`** (`lib/close-out-events-store.js`). Bounded to `{urlKey, merged:true, prMergedAt ≥ since}`, newest first, capped at 500. It projects three fields and swallows errors to `[]`, like `listForIssue`. It keeps LIN-3713's named unindexed shape and the `db-indexes.js` comment says so. The producer does stamp `prMergedAt`: `lib/close-out-merges.js:63/82` passes `status.merged_at` (LIN-3756).
- **Wiring.** `server.js:3279` → `createProxyRoutes` → `createComputeRoutes`. The store exists at `server.js:849`. There is a source-reading witness plus a warn-once when the store is missing. Builder note 1 is met.
- **Fold.** `foldPeriodicalRuns` is still pure and takes landings as data. `landed` applies only on the cadence branch when the lane would read `recent`. That excludes queued rows (rule 1) and `due`, and the fold checks `scope:'repo'`, newer than last run, and ≥ `LANDED_MIN_GAP_MS`. The null lane matches any repo. Named lanes match `owner/name` or bare name, case-insensitive. The top level reads `landed` only when it would read `recent`.
- **Self-exclusion (B1).** `issueIdentifier` was added to `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION`, and the history projection inherits it by spread. The comment beside `_periodicalIssues` names the LIN-2575 dependency as asked.
- **Also update.** Done: `proxy-instructions.js`, the source map, the kickoff first act ("rank it as `recent`" until LIN-4382), and removal of the `routes/proxy.js` dead imports (note 5). **One listing was missed:** `docs/proxy-integration.md:1477`. See the fix below.
- **Out of scope respected.** No changes to `render-observation.js`, `public/observation.js`, hooks or the scheduler.
- **Acceptance.** `tests/unit/periodical-runs.test.js` is unchanged and passes. All seven named fold cases exist. The route-level real-store witness exists. The production wiring witness exists. The pre-check outcome is recorded on LIN-4349, as "unobservable".

### Regression check
`git log` on the touched store/fold files shows LIN-3713/LIN-3756 (the `prMergedAt` recording that this read depends on) intact, and no reverts. Main moved after the ticket was created (LIN-4370 touched `routes/proxy*.js`). The PR is rebased onto it and CI is green.

### Test quality: mutation checks (each reverted, tree clean)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| drop `issueIdentifier` from `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION` | 5 fail (incl. real-store route test) |
| drop the one-day gap guard | 1 fail |
| drop the self-exclusion `continue` | 3 fail |
| drop the `scope:'repo'` guard | 1 fail |
| drop `closeOutEventsStore` from server.js's `createProxyRoutes` call | 1 fail |
| drop "merged after last run" | 2 fail |
| null-lane matching → match everything | 2 fail |
| top-level `landed` aggregation removed | 5 fail |
| `listMergedSince` without `merged:true` | 1 fail |

Test level fits the change: a pure-fold unit, a real-store route test, and a source-reading wiring check. Locally, the 172 tests across the six relevant files pass.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "places that list the Periodical lane-state union". I searched lib, routes, public, prompts and docs. Every listing was updated except `docs/proxy-integration.md` §`GET /api/proxy/periodicals`, which is **inside** (same class as the ticket's "Also update … the state union"). The rendering consumers are explicitly out of scope. There's no `### Leftovers` comment, and I found no other leftover edges.

**Fix for close-out (on the PR branch):** in `docs/proxy-integration.md:1477`, change "is one of four values" to "is one of five values" and add a `"landed"` clause after the `"due"` clause:
> `"landed"` (LIN-4381) — a lane that would read `"recent"` has had a PR merge in its repo (by forge merge time) since its last run, at least a day after it, on a repo-scoped template with no queued run; a merge on an issue a Periodical row names doesn't count, and `"due"` always wins. The top level reads `"landed"` when it would read `"recent"` and any lane does.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **1. Merged close-out events are actually recorded live, with `prMergedAt` (the ticket's pre-check). Inside: a claim this change depends on, and the pre-check is in the ticket.** Without them, `landed` never fires and nothing complains, because the route fails toward `recent`. **Before the merge:** someone with owner/DB access reads `close-out-events` for `{issueIdentifier:'LIN-4376', merged:true}`, or opens LIN-4376's task page. Right = an event exists with a non-null `prMergedAt` and a `prUrl` for PR #2361. Wrong = no event, or `prMergedAt` null. If it's wrong, the recording fix is in scope on this ticket (back to `bug`/`implementation`), not a filing. **After the deploy:** the first proxy-written Done of a merged PR whose repo lane has been idle more than a day shows that lane `landed` in `GET /api/proxy/periodicals` (plan risk 4; don't count one miss, per builder note 3).
- **2. Self-exclusion holds in production: Stage-2 review dispatches carry `periodicalId`. Inside: B1, the claim the exclusion depends on.** Only the recommend-and-dispatch descent (`routes/proxy.js:1574`) and the override arm (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1583`) derive it from the gate marker. A Stage-2 dispatched any other way (session UI dispatch, a plain `POST /dispatch` without `periodicalId`) would not be excluded. Its self-merged notes PR would then make lanes `landed` again, bounded only by the one-day gap. **Before the merge:** for the most recent Periodical review issues (e.g. LIN-4379/LIN-4380's Seams & Tangles and corrective reads, or any gate-marked issue run in the last 30 days), `GET /api/proxy/dispatch?issueIdentifier=<review issue>` shows the run rows with a non-null `periodicalId`. Right = every Stage-2 row stamped. Wrong = any Stage-2 row with `periodicalId: null`. **After the deploy:** after the next Periodical Stage-2 self-merge, its template's lanes stay `recent`, not `landed`, in `GET /api/proxy/periodicals`.
- **3. `docs/proxy-integration.md` state union. Inside.** Settled before the merge by close-out making the fix above.

**Rollback:** revert PR #2376's merge commit. Nothing is persisted in a new shape (a read-only read plus a projection field), and the only consumer of `landed` (the kickoff) ranks it as `recent`.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

**LIN-4381 close-out: ledger state before the merge (PR #2376, head `4fd695e0`, CI 7/7 green on that commit)**

- **Item 3 (docs state union): settled.** Commit `4fd695e0` changes `docs/proxy-integration.md` §`GET /api/proxy/periodicals` from "four values" to "five values" and adds review's `"landed"` clause verbatim.
- **Item 2 (Stage-2 rows carry `periodicalId`): settled pre-merge, with evidence.** The proxy's dispatch reads don't project `periodicalId`, so I used the fold's own output. In live `GET /api/proxy/periodicals`, each recent template's `lastDispatchedAt` equals a Stage-2 row whose `promptName` matches no template title. `_resolveTemplateForRow` can join such a row only through `periodicalId`:
  - seams-tangles `12:59:53.739Z` = LIN-4387's `close-out` row `b04877d0` (the run that merges the notes PR);
  - design-review `14:24:04.308Z` = LIN-4391's `plan-review` row `f1e7a8b3`;
  - comprehension-debt `2026-11-05T19:36:56.050Z` = LIN-4300's `research` row `6ab0b66c`;
  - stability-review `2026-11-04T08:31:38.128Z` = LIN-4206's `review` row `be36b526`.
  
  All four autopilot-run review issues therefore have at least one stamped Stage-2 row, which is what `_periodicalIssues` needs: one row naming the issue excludes every landing on it. The proxy can't show whether *every* row is stamped (only the newest done row surfaces), and the exclusion doesn't depend on that. A Stage-2 dispatched entirely outside the kickoff/recommend paths would still be unexcluded; this is the residual review named, bounded by the one-day gap.
- **Item 1 (merged events recorded live with `prMergedAt`): pre-merge read not possible from here; settled by the post-deploy read instead.** This session reaches only `/api/proxy/*`, which has no `close-out-events` reader, and has no DB access (same finding as LIN-4349 `68476ed5`). Engineering call: merge, and witness it post-deploy through the new read itself. Reasons:
  - The post-deploy read is a strictly stronger test of the same claim. Four repo-scoped lanes are `recent` with their last run over a day old: code-quality and stability-review (11-04), comprehension-debt (11-05) and drift-coherence (11-06). Non-Periodical PRs have merged since (#2361, #2375, #2370). So on deploy those lanes must read `landed` if and only if merged events with `prMergedAt` are recorded for this workspace.
  - The merge risks nothing in the meantime. The read is read-only and fails toward `recent`, and the kickoff ranks `landed` as `recent` until LIN-4382.
  - A recording fix wouldn't touch this PR's code either way.
  
  If those lanes stay `recent` after the deploy, this ticket stays open and the recording fix is done here, at its cause, as review specified.

## Close-out — LIN-4381

**Merged:** PR [#2376](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2376), merge commit `3272fe4a6d92defc172c9e2c7081f48ddc991cb0` (2026-11-08T15:01:51Z), pinned with `--match-head-commit` to head `4fd695e0`. **Deployed:** the harbour.cat footer shows `3272fe4a`.

**How it meets what was asked:** as review recorded (comment `02ad1bea`):
- the bounded `listMergedSince` read;
- `closeOutEventsStore` wired through `server.js` → `createProxyRoutes` → `createComputeRoutes`, with a source-reading witness;
- the pure fold with `landed` and all five guards;
- B1 self-exclusion through `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION.issueIdentifier`;
- every state-union listing updated, scope respected;
- all named fold cases, the real-store route witness and the wiring witness present;
- `tests/unit/periodical-runs.test.js` unchanged.

Nine mutation checks were each caught.

**Changes made at close-out**
- `4fd695e0`: `docs/proxy-integration.md` §`GET /api/proxy/periodicals`, from "four values" to "five values", plus review's `"landed"` clause. This answers review's "Fix for close-out" and ledger item 3.
- No other code changes. Main hadn't moved past `f0388614`, so no rebase was needed.

**Ledger**
1. **Merged close-out events recorded live with `prMergedAt`: settled post-deploy, by observation.**
   - The pre-merge read (owner/DB) wasn't reachable from a proxy-only session. Comment `31bfbaef` records the call to witness it through the new read instead, and why.
   - After the deploy, `GET /api/proxy/periodicals` shows exactly the predicted lanes as `landed`: code-quality, stability-review, comprehension-debt and drift-coherence. These are the repo-scoped lanes that were `recent` with their last run more than a day old. Before the deploy (same read at ~14:55Z, on `f0388614`) all four read `recent`.
   - `listMergedSince` returns only `{merged:true, prMergedAt ≥ since}` rows, so merged events with `prMergedAt` are being recorded for this workspace.
   - Control: the lanes run today stay `recent` because of the one-day gap (design-review 14:24Z, seams-tangles 12:59Z). `due` lanes stay `due`.
   - Plan risk 4 ("`landed` never fires") is answered for the fold: it fires. The P4 precedence half stays with LIN-4382.
   - The specific LIN-4376 / #2361 row wasn't read individually. This aggregate witness covers the claim the change depends on, so no recording fix was needed.
2. **Stage-2 rows carry `periodicalId` (B1): settled pre-merge with evidence** (comment `31bfbaef`).
   - In each case the fold joined a row through `periodicalId` alone, because its `promptName` matches no template title:
     - LIN-4387 `close-out` `b04877d0` → seams-tangles;
     - LIN-4391 `plan-review` `f1e7a8b3` → design-review;
     - LIN-4300 `research` `6ab0b66c` → comprehension-debt;
     - LIN-4206 `review` `be36b526` → stability-review.
   - Every recent review issue is therefore named by a stamped row, which is all `_periodicalIssues` needs.
   - **Post-deploy self-merge check: not run conclusively.**
     - What: a Periodical's own merge leaves lanes `recent`.
     - Why not: its own template's lane is always inside the one-day gap at its self-merge, so `recent` there doesn't distinguish anything. The cross-template form needs a moment when a Periodical's merge is the only landing after some lane's last run. Today other PRs have landed, and four lanes read `landed` from them.
     - Who can run it: anyone with proxy read, after a quiet stretch when a Periodical review merges, by checking that idle repo lanes don't flip to `landed`. Or an owner, by checking `close-out-events` for that issue against the fold.
     - The exclusion logic itself is witnessed by the real-store route test, which fails with the projection grant removed.
3. **`docs/proxy-integration.md` state union: settled** by `4fd695e0`.

**Rollback (named by review):** revert merge commit `3272fe4a`. No new persisted shape.

**Final CI:** 7/7 green on `4fd695e0`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan (source), CI success (run 42491895482).

**Related tickets:** LIN-4382 (P4) was blocked by this and is now unblocked; left in Todo for its own run. LIN-4349's pre-check outcome is updated there. No outside items were in the ledger, so no follow-ups were filed.

## Autopilot run summary — LIN-4381 (stepper, model opus throughout)

**Beats (one warm session, kind implementation):** 1/4 ground + pre-check + branch (`66b3c477`) → 2/4 merged-events read, wiring, `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION` (`dbb42ee1`) → 3/4 `landed` fold, self-exclusion, witnesses (`75695fe1`) → 4/4 docs, PR, CI (`cc9f8cff`). Then engine-routed `review` (`c1db8868`, conditional Approve, comment `02ad1bea`) and `close-out` (`c7fb9742`).

**Verified by me, not by report:**
- PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2376 is MERGED (merge commit `3272fe4a6d92defc172c9e2c7081f48ddc991cb0`, 2026-11-08T15:01:51Z).
- CI on that merge commit: CI success, Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan, all success. CI was also 7/7 green on the reviewed head `d4117ba7`.
- LIN-4381 state is Done. The pre-existing test file the PR touched (`tests/unit/proxy-periodicals-route.test.js`) only gained additions; `tests/unit/periodical-runs.test.js` is unchanged (79/79).
- Witnesses were each seen failing first (builder), and review reran nine mutations, each caught.

**Decisions I settled (engineering):** a top-level `landed` can read while another lane has a queued run (spec-literal; the per-lane state is authoritative); the 30-day exclusion window gap is documented in code (a Periodical's own PR merges after its run row).

**What holds / what's left:** after deploy, the four predicted repo-scoped lanes read `landed` (close-out comment `bac89834`), which witnesses live merged-event recording; the LIN-4376 row itself was not read individually. The post-deploy self-merge check was not run conclusively (recorded in close-out with what/why/who). Precedence for `landed` in the kickoff is LIN-4382's.

issue.title: LIN-4349 P2: the other 12 corrective Periodicals feed the notes and mint nothing
